title: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education - National Value Education - Supremacy of Constitution
exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
subject: National Value Education

questions.q: The principle of the **Supremacy of the Constitution** simply means that:
options: The military forces have supreme control over the laws of the country
The Constitution is the highest law of the land, and all other laws and persons are subject to it
The President can single-handedly alter the fundamental rights of citizens
Only wealthy and influential citizens are above the constitutional laws
questions.explain: The **Supremacy of the Constitution** dictates that the constitution is the supreme and highest law of the land. Everyone, including the government and its citizens, must obey it.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: Under the principle of Constitutional Supremacy, what happens if any regular law made by the National Assembly contradicts a provision of the Constitution?
options: The Constitution is amended immediately to fit the new law
The new law overrides the Constitution because it is more recent
The new law becomes null and void to the extent of its inconsistency
The National Assembly is dissolved automatically by the judiciary
questions.explain: Because the Constitution is supreme, any other law that contradicts it is deemed invalid, or **null and void**, to the extent of that contradiction.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: Who among the following is entirely exempt from obeying a supreme constitution in a fully democratic state?
options: The President of the country
The Chief Justice
The Inspector General of Police
No one is exempt
questions.explain: In a democratic system governed by constitutional supremacy, **no individual, leader, or institution** is above the law. Everyone is equally subject to the dictates of the constitution.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: The Supremacy of the Constitution works hand-in-hand with which major democratic pillar to ensure equality before the law?
options: The Rule of Law
Gerrymandering
Oligarchy
Absolute Monarchy
questions.explain: The **Rule of Law** is fundamentally intertwined with the supremacy of the constitution, as both concepts emphasize that all individuals are equal before the highest law of the state.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: Which of the following is a primary benefit of constitutional supremacy in a nation?
options: It strictly concentrates all absolute powers into the hands of one dictator
It prevents arbitrary rule and protects the fundamental rights of citizens
It completely abolishes the existence of local governments
It allows electoral malpractice to go unpunished
questions.explain: By keeping leaders in check and defining the limits of their powers, constitutional supremacy **prevents dictatorial (arbitrary) rule** and effectively guards citizens' rights.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: In a Federal system like Nigeria, how does the supremacy of the constitution aid in governance?
options: By clearly defining and sharing powers among the Federal, State, and Local governments to prevent conflict
By forcing State governments to permanently surrender their budgets to foreign organizations
By ensuring the central government can unlawfully imprison state governors
By encouraging violent succession of power
questions.explain: In a federation, a supreme written constitution is crucial because it acts as a legally binding document that strictly **shares and defines the powers** among the various tiers of government, thereby preventing boundary conflicts and abuse of power.
